correctness.rationale: For n>=7, the graph-square cliques have exactly 3n maximal tetrahedra of three explicitly described cyclic families. Nine orbitwise elementary free-face phases each delete 2n faces, leaving the n lower vertices and n consecutive lower edges. Critical hypotheses n>=7, graph distance, and inclusive threshold two are explicit. The pure-stdlib verifier independently enumerates actual Rips faces and replays every pair n=7,...,20; the uniform local facet classification and phase incidence checks, rather than these samples, prove the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The cycle-square/thickened cylindrical graph is a natural finite graph-metric Rips family, arising as equally spaced samples of a circular ladder. Exact 9n simplicial collapse onto a specified rim gives an infinite-family strong homotopy classification and integral homology rather than a computed Betti sequence. The scale-two behavior is distinguished from the cubical small case and the continuous graph literature.
